entries.title: Exodus 26:1
segments: Tabernacle; the words tabernacle and tent are sometimes used in a general way to denote the whole structure of the movable temple described in the present chapter,
. But in a strict sense, the tabernacle is always the inner set of curtains described in
while the tent is the covering above it of goats' hair.  See

. 
 
  Cherubim of cunning work; or rather, the work of a cunning deviser. It is generally agreed that these curtains were woven with different colors and figures of cherubim, while the hanging for the door of the tent,
, was embroidered.

entries.title: Exodus 26:3
segments: Coupled together; in the Hebrew simply joined.  Hence a great curtain formed from the union of several smaller curtains is called a joining, or "coupling."

entries.title: Exodus 26:4
segments:
The edge of the one curtain; that is of the one great curtain. 
 
  From the selvedge in the coupling; rather, on the edge in the coupling.  The coupling is the compound curtain made of five single curtains. 
 
  In the uttermost edge--coupling of the second; or, in the edge of the outermost curtain in the second coupling.  The simple meaning is, that in the edge of the outermost curtain of each coupling (compound curtain) on the adjacent sides should be loops, etc., corresponding to each other.

entries.title: Exodus 26:5
segments: Coupling of the second; or, second coupling.  See note

. 
 
  Take hold one of another; or, be opposite one to another.

entries.title: Exodus 26:6
segments: Taches; clasps to unite the loops, and thus the edges of the curtains.

entries.title: Exodus 26:9
segments: Double; double it over in an ornamental way.

entries.title: Exodus 26:10
segments: Which coupleth the second; or, in respect to the second coupling. See note

entries.title: Exodus 26:12
segments: The half curtain that remaineth; that is, the half of the second great curtain made of five single curtains.  The framework of shittim-wood was thirty cubits long and ten cubits high.  The two great curtains of goats' hair, when united, made a covering 44 cubits long by 30 wide.  Of this, 4 cubits were doubled over in front; 30 more were needed to cover the framework; leaving 10 cubits, that is just half of the second great curtain, to hang over in the rear.

entries.title: Exodus 26:13
segments: That which remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent; that in which the curtains of the tent exceed in length those of the tabernacle.  Here the sacred writer reckons according to the length of a single curtain.  The curtains of the inner covering (tabernacle) were 28 cubits long; those of the outer covering (tent) were 30 cubits in length.  When the two coverings were spread over the framework of shittim-wood, so that the curtains, regarded as single, lay across it and hung down on each side, the curtains of the tent must have extended just a cubit on each side below the curtains of the tabernacle, so as entirely to cover the latter.

entries.title: Exodus 26:15
segments: Boards; with the exception of
, where the meaning is uncertain, the word here rendered "boards" is used only of the framework of the sanctuary.  It does not denote common boards, but rather thick planks.  See on

entries.title: Exodus 26:17
segments: Tenons; projections to set into the sockets of silver.

entries.title: Exodus 26:22
segments: Six boards; it is generally agreed that the width of the tabernacle on the inner side was ten cubits.  The Jewish rabbins agree in representing the planks, or timbers, of the tabernacle to have been one cubit in thickness.  As they were a cubit and a half in width, this would require just eight to reach from outside to outside on the western end.  If they had a less thickness, then the two corner planks,
, must have extended just so far beyond the side.

entries.title: Exodus 26:24
segments:
Coupled together; in the Hebrew, twinned, that is made double.  The meaning seems to be, that each corner-plank shall be joined above and below to the adjacent side-plank, so that the two shall make a pair. 
 
  Unto one ring; so that one ring shall serve to unite the two.

entries.title: Exodus 26:26
segments: Bars; these were to run through the sides of the framework, to increase its strength.

entries.title: Exodus 26:30
segments: In order to be accepted, we must consecrate to God the best that we have, and be careful in all things to follow his directions.

entries.title: Exodus 26:33
segments: The holy place and the most holy; these were the two divisions into which the tabernacle was divided; the holy place being twenty cubits by ten, and the holy of holies ten cubits square.

. 
 
As the veil which separated the holy from the most holy place, in the tabernacle and afterwards in the temple, was at the crucifixion of Christ rent in twain, to show us that the way to the throne of mercy is open for all, all should, with believing and grateful hearts, draw near to God, in that new and living way opened by the death of Christ, that they may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in all times of need.

entries.title: Exodus 26:36
segments: The door; the entrance to the tabernacle, which was on the east.
